So I finally tried making sourdough last weekend, and wow, what a mess. I'd been putting it off for months because honestly it seemed like way too much fuss. My friend Dana swears by hers, sends me photos of these gorgeous loaves, and I figured how hard can it be?

Turns out, pretty hard. The starter smelled weird on day three and I almost threw the whole thing out. But I stuck with it. By day five it was bubbling away and smelled kind of nice, a little sour, a little yeasty.

The first loaf? Flat as a pancake. Dense too. I think I killed the yeast with water that was too hot. My partner ate a slice to be polite and made a face he thought I didn't see.

Second try went better. I was more careful this time, kept the water lukewarm, and let it rise overnight in the fridge. When I pulled it out the next morning it had actually doubled. Baking it filled the kitchen with that warm bread smell, you know the one.

It wasn't perfect. The crust was a bit pale and the crumb was tighter than I wanted. But it was bread, real bread, and I made it with my own two hands. I texted Dana a photo and she sent back about fifteen exclamation marks. I'm hooked now. Already planning the next batch.
